text:
### Observed differences

- The elapsed time between consecutive completion events for the activity pair A28 and A32 roughly halved. In the earlier window it averaged about 1.0 hours (median about 1.0; the middle half of the 200 traces fell between roughly 0.9 and 1.1 hours), while in the later window it averaged about 0.5 hours (median about 0.5; middle half roughly 0.44–0.54 hours) — a drop of about 0.53 hours, or roughly half. [TWAIT001]
- The gap also became more consistent: its standard deviation fell from about 0.18 hours to about 0.09 hours, and every summarised component (mean, median, both quartiles, spread) moved down together. [TWAIT001]
- This difference rests on all 200 traces in each window and is larger than in about 999.5 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data, so it is unusual for a split with no change. [TWAIT001]
- No structural difference qualified: 0 of 54 tested control-flow units passed screening, in line with the roughly 0.27 items expected by chance in an unchanged process. [screening]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Although the timing gap between A28 and A32 halved and is based on every trace in both windows, it is a single qualifying item in a family where about 0.006 items were expected by chance — a count an unchanged process can still occasionally produce — and no structural or relational evidence corroborates it.
